describes: The settings of single tools: the thresholds, minimum samples and scope of the coverage and mutation gate and the files it mutates as Commands (`threshold*`, `mutationCommands`; the header of `scripts/check-thresholds.mjs`); how long HEAD must sit still in a worktree before `scripts/prune-worktree-branches.mjs` removes it, on every host, unless a caller names it with `--finished` or its branch with `--discard`, how many merged pull requests that sweep reads from GitHub and how long it waits for them (`worktreeGc*`); how much of a failing job's output the git hook runner, `scripts/git-hooks.mjs`, prints (`gitHooksFailedOutputBytes`); the longest one call of `scripts/fresh-run.mjs` may take (`freshRunDeadlineSeconds`); the model `scripts/code-graph.mjs` extracts the documents and names the communities with when it builds the local code graph, with the graphify release the `pypi:graphifyy` pin in `mise.toml` names, the file types whose items it stamps as semantic, the folder it builds into, the name it registers the MCP server under, and the file beside the graph that the harness assessment writes the combined graph to and that the server is registered on while it is current, with the field in it that records the graph it was built from (`graphify*`); how the co-change map of `tools/coupling/coupling.ts` reads the trunk's merged pull requests: the committer address of a merge, the paths it ignores, its rename similarity, the most files a counted pull request may change, and the thresholds of an edge, a rate's sample, a hub and a cluster (`coupling*`); the platforms the toolchain's lockfile, `mise.lock`, covers (`toolchainLockPlatforms`); and the model every TypeSafe question is sent to and the thresholds, skip list, passage sizes, width, cap and offline share of `mise run citations:support` (`typesafeModel`, `citationSupport*`). It holds, too, the threshold of `mise run prompts:incidents` and the fewest words of a paragraph it judges (`promptIncident*`), which reads `typesafeModel` as well; and the agents' GitHub App, its installation, the one repository a token `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` mints may reach and the account that owns it, which the dev container clones, how much of a kept token's hour must be left for it to hand the token out again, and the App's bot account the dev container commits as (`githubApp*`). And it holds the Langfuse projects `scripts/prompt-run-figures.mjs` reads a pending run's figures from, with the environment variables of their keys, the endpoint and field groups it asks for, its page size, the names it counts turns and tool calls by, the usage keys each token figure sums and the one Langfuse adds as their sum, how far back a window opens, and how long and how often it waits on the API (`langfuse*`).
whyThisFileExists: Each of these belongs to one tool, unlike the rest of the policy, and a constant a tool reads still lives in a policy file under a key, with its reason beside it (`AGENTS.md` § Three kinds of file, and never a fourth). They share one record under `policy/` rather than one beside each tool, so every tunable of the workflow is in one directory (`docs/decisions.md` § D-27). The harness keeps its own record beside it, `tools/harness/harness.config.json`, for the reason `docs/decisions.md` § D-26 gives: its constants are what changes when it is pointed at another harness. That record names six keys here it reads, `couplingMinSampleUnits`, `couplingClusterMinJaccardPermille`, `graphifySemanticExtensions`, `graphifyOutDir`, `graphifyCombinedGraphFile` and `graphifyCombinedGraphBlobField`, and copies none.
gatedBy: mise run check:policy holds this record's header, a `Means` beside every constant, and no key another record also defines. mise run thresholds:check and mise run thresholds:commands:check hold `thresholdPercents`, `thresholdMinSamples`, `thresholdScope` and `mutationCommands`: they refuse any of the four missing, of the wrong shape or with no `Means` sibling, and judge the branch's changed code by their values; mise run thresholds:selftest runs each refusal on a fixture repository carrying a copy of the policy, sized from its minimum samples, and one with the keys removed. mise run worktree:selftest holds `worktreeGcMinAgeHours`: with the liveness check working, a worktree between an agent's calls, and one whose branch's pull request has merged, are kept by the key's reason while HEAD there has been still less than it, one still past it is removed, and one its caller names with `--finished`, or whose branch it names with `--discard`, is removed at once; with the liveness check forced off and the key unreadable, an idle worktree is kept. mise run worktree:selftest holds `worktreeGcMergedPrLimit` as the limit a stub `gh` is asked for; no gate holds `worktreeGcGhTimeoutSeconds`, which bounds a call to GitHub that no gate makes. mise run hooks:selftest holds `gitHooksFailedOutputBytes`: it refuses a policy without the key or its `Means` sibling, and asserts that a failing job's printed output stops at the key's value while a file holds all of it; the runner refuses to start a commit or a push without it. No gate holds the value of `freshRunDeadlineSeconds`: `scripts/fresh-run.mjs` refuses a run without it, and mise run tests:fresh:selftest runs its deadline case through the caller's own deadline instead. mise run citations:support:selftest holds `typesafeModel` and the eight `citationSupport*` keys: it refuses a run whose policy lacks one, or one of their `Means` siblings, or whose threshold or offline share is over 1, and holds both thresholds as inclusive, the skip list, the passage sizes, the cap and the offline fallback a missing key runs; `citations:support` itself reads a token and the network and no gate runs it. `mise run code-graph` reads the six `graphify*` keys, and graphify's release from the `pypi:graphifyy` pin in `mise.toml`, and no job runs it, since it reads the network, a language model and the person's own plan. mise run code-graph:selftest, at pre-push and in CI, runs it against stub tools with the policy's values: it fails on a policy missing any of the six, and holds the `mise.toml` pin as the release the script requires, `graphifyClaudeCliModel` as the model passed to extraction and naming, `graphifyOutDir` as the folder graphify is told to write, `graphifyMcpServerName` as the name registered, and `graphifyCombinedGraphFile` as the file registered when its `graphifyCombinedGraphBlobField` records the graph beside it. mise run harness:selftest holds `graphifyCombinedGraphFile` as the file `tools/harness/graph.py` writes, beside the graph it combines, and `graphifyCombinedGraphBlobField` as the field it records that graph's blob id under, from a fixture record whose field is not this one. No gate holds `graphifySemanticExtensions` to graphify's own list of file types, which lives outside this repository. mise run coupling:check holds the eight `coupling*` keys and reads `prReviewMergeMethod` of `policy/pr-review.json`: it refuses a key missing, without its `Means` sibling or of the wrong shape, and a merge method other than `rebase`, and re-derives the co-change map by their values; mise run coupling:selftest runs each refusal on a fixture repository carrying a copy of the policy with those keys set to the fixture's own, and holds that the live values have the shapes the check reads. mise run harness:selftest reads the six keys `tools/harness/harness.config.json` names from fixture records of its own. mise run check:toolchain holds `mise.lock` to `toolchainLockPlatforms`, refusing a tool with no URL and checksum for one of them, and refuses a policy without the key; mise run check:toolchain:selftest runs that refusal on a copy of the policy given a platform the lock does not cover. mise run prompts:incidents:selftest holds `typesafeModel` and the two `promptIncident*` keys: it refuses a run whose policy lacks one or its `Means` sibling, whose threshold is over 1, or whose fewest words is not a whole number of at least 1, and holds the threshold as inclusive and the fewest words as the least a paragraph sent holds; `prompts:incidents` itself reads a token and the network and no gate runs it. mise run github-app-token:selftest holds the seven `githubApp*` keys. It runs `.devcontainer/entrypoint.sh`'s `clone`, which reads `githubAppRepositoryOwner` and `githubAppTokenRepository` for the clone it makes at a container's first start, against a local repository at the address they give, and refuses with its reason a policy without the owner. It also refuses a policy without `githubAppId` or `githubAppTokenRepository`, or with a `githubAppTokenRefreshSeconds` of 0, by its reason; it holds the identity `identity` prints as made, in GitHub's noreply form, from `githubAppBotLogin` and `githubAppBotUserId`, whatever their values, and refuses a policy without either; it holds the JSON Web Token as signed for the App `githubAppId` names, and the request as made for the installation `githubAppInstallationId` names and for `githubAppTokenRepository` alone, before a stub of GitHub's endpoint; and it holds a kept token with less than `githubAppTokenRefreshSeconds` left as replaced. No gate holds the App's two ids to GitHub, which only a token minted from the App's key can read, nor the bot account's login and id, which GitHub's users endpoint gives, nor the owner to the repository's: the high-risk floor holds all five, through `githubApp*` in `prReviewHighRiskJsonKeys`, to a person. mise run prompt-runs:figures:selftest holds the thirteen `langfuse*` keys: it runs `scripts/prompt-run-figures.mjs` against a stub of Langfuse's API on loopback with the live values but `langfuseBaseUrl`, pointed at the stub, and `langfusePageLimit`, set to 2 or to 3; it holds the field groups as the ones every request asks for, the projects' variables as the keys each is read with, the turn name, the tool-name prefix, the usage buckets and Langfuse's total key as the figures it works by hand, over rows of its own and over the rows of the second read in asdlc-openspec-ic9h.10, the lookback as the start of a window with no earlier analysis, and the retry limit, the longest wait and the timeout as the failures each gives; and it refuses a policy without `langfuseProjects`, field groups naming `io` or without `usage`, a base URL over http to a host that is not loopback or with a path, an observations path of `//host` or `/\host`, a usage key in two buckets, the total key in a bucket, and two projects naming one variable. No gate holds `langfuseBaseUrl`, the projects or the plugin's names to Langfuse itself, which only a live read sees, in the probe dispatch of asdlc-openspec-ic9h.11; the high-risk floor holds the `langfuse*` keys to a person.
gitHooksFailedOutputBytesMeans: The most bytes of a failing job's output that the hook runner, `scripts/git-hooks.mjs`, prints at a commit, a push or `mise run gates`: the last ones, where a failure's summary is, followed by the path of a file under the temporary directory that holds all of it. A passing job prints one line. Without it one failing job can print past what an agent's tool output holds, which lefthook did (`asdlc-openspec-pp6`, hazard 4): on 2026-10-01 its run with one failing job printed 110,244 bytes, and the harness cut it mid-run. Sized from that day's passing run (`asdlc-openspec-uc1`, step 0d): the largest job printed 23,593 bytes (workflows-selftest), the next two 9,590 and 9,331, and the other 29 under 7 KB each, so three failures print about 25 KB. Raising it shows more of a large failure in one read; lowering it fits more failures in one. Where it loses: workflows-selftest failing on an early case, whose FAIL line sits more than 8 KB before its end, needs a second read of the file, where no cap would have shown it at once. Decided 2026-10-01 by the maintainer, D3 of asdlc-openspec-uc1, from a recommendation put with that case.
githubAppIdMeans: The id of the agents' GitHub App (`docs/decisions.md` § D-51), which `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` puts as the `iss` of the JSON Web Token it signs with the App's private key when it asks GitHub for an installation token for the dev container's `git` and `gh`. Recorded by asdlc-openspec-owva.2 on 2026-10-05, from the App's settings page. GitHub checks the token's signature against the public key of the App this names, so a wrong id, or another App's with this App's key, gets every token refused, and the helper prints GitHub's answer. Where it loses: a fork, or a maintainer with an App of their own, mints nothing until a pull request changes this.
githubAppBotLoginMeans: The login of the agents' GitHub App's bot account, which the dev container commits as: `scripts/github-app-token.mjs identity` prints it as `user.name`, and `.devcontainer/entrypoint.sh` sets that in the container's `~/.gitconfig` at start when no `user.email` is set. Read 2026-10-06 from `gh api /users/asdlc-agent-j%5Bbot%5D`, which gave type Bot (asdlc-openspec-irvc). A wrong login gives commits a name that is not the App's, while `githubAppBotUserId` still ties them to the account through the email. Where it loses: an App renamed on GitHub keeps committing under the old name until this is edited, and a container whose `~/.gitconfig` was set before the edit keeps it until a rebuild discards that file, since the entrypoint leaves an email already set.
githubAppBotUserIdMeans: The id of that bot account, not the App's id (`githubAppId`): `scripts/github-app-token.mjs identity` makes `user.email` from it as `<this>+<githubAppBotLogin>@users.noreply.github.com`, the form GitHub documents for an account's noreply address (docs.github.com, "Email addresses reference", read 2026-10-06). GitHub attributes a commit with that email to the bot account, through a rename too, since the id is in it. Read 2026-10-06 from `gh api /users/asdlc-agent-j%5Bbot%5D` (asdlc-openspec-irvc). Where it loses: a commit is not signed by it, so GitHub shows no Verified badge on the container's commits, which only a commit the App creates through the API gets.
githubAppInstallationIdMeans: The installation of that App on this repository, whose installation token `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` asks for at `/app/installations/<this>/access_tokens`. A token asked for with no body reaches every repository the installation covers: asdlc-openspec-owva.2 asked for this one alone, and on 2026-10-06 such a token, minted in the dev container, listed 8 of the maintainer's repositories, this one among them (`gh api /installation/repositories`). The helper therefore asks for `githubAppTokenRepository` alone. The maintainer narrowed the installation to this repository alone the same day, in its settings on GitHub. asdlc-openspec-t4cz's note of 2026-10-06 records that on their word, not from a command: every token the helper mints names this one repository, so `gh api /installation/repositories` lists it alone whether the installation covers 1 repository or 8, and only a token minted from the App's key with no body lists what the installation covers. Added 2026-10-07 (asdlc-openspec-t4cz). Recorded by asdlc-openspec-owva.2 on 2026-10-05, from the App's settings page. Where it loses: an App uninstalled and installed again gets a new id, and every token is refused until this is edited.
githubAppTokenRepositoryMeans: The bootstrapped project sets this to its own repository's bare name; `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` refuses the placeholder as not a repository's bare name, and `.devcontainer/entrypoint.sh` clones nothing while it stands. The one repository, by its bare name, that a token `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` mints may reach: it sends `{"repositories": [<this>]}` with each request, which GitHub documents as narrowing that one token to the repositories named, among those the installation covers (docs.github.com, "Create an installation access token for an app", read 2026-10-06). This repository, since the dev container's sessions work here and its tracker's Dolt remote is here too (`.beads/config.yaml`). Without it, every token reached the 8 repositories the installation covered on 2026-10-06 (`githubAppInstallationIdMeans`). Where it loses: it narrows the tokens the helper mints, and no other: a session can read the App's key, which the container mounts for it, and mint a token for every repository the installation covers. On the maintainer's word, the installation covers this repository alone since 2026-10-06 (`githubAppInstallationIdMeans`), so `githubAppTokenRepository` and the installation name the same repository. A repository later added to the installation on GitHub is open to such a token at once, and no gate reads the installation's list to see it. Added 2026-10-07 (asdlc-openspec-t4cz). Decided 2026-10-06 (asdlc-openspec-owva.4), from its adversarial review's finding, which a skeptic upheld.
githubAppRepositoryOwnerMeans: The bootstrapped project sets this to the account that owns its repository; `.devcontainer/entrypoint.sh` refuses the placeholder and clones nothing while it stands. The account that owns `githubAppTokenRepository`, which the App is installed on. `.devcontainer/entrypoint.sh` clones `https://github.com/<this>/<githubAppTokenRepository>.git` into the container's workspace volume at its first start, with no token, since the repository is public (`gh repo view --json visibility`, 2026-10-06). It reads both keys from the copy of this record `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` puts in the image, because the clone that holds this file does not exist yet (docs/decisions.md § D-54). A changed value reaches a container only once it is rebuilt, and only one whose volume holds no clone yet. Where it loses: the high-risk floor holds it to a person through `githubApp*`, because a wrong value clones another account's code into every new container, where the entrypoint runs `npm ci` and its hooks. Recorded 2026-10-06 (asdlc-openspec-vvns), from `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`.
githubAppTokenRefreshSecondsMeans: How many seconds of a kept installation token's life must be left for `scripts/github-app-token.mjs` to hand it out again; with fewer, it mints a fresh one and keeps that. GitHub's installation token lasts an hour (docs.github.com, "Generating an installation access token for a GitHub App", read 2026-10-06), and `git` and `gh` each read a token once, when a command starts, so a command must end before the token it read expires. 1800 gives every command at least half an hour, which holds a watcher run in the background, such as `gh pr checks --watch` while `verify` runs, and costs one call to GitHub each half hour a session works. Raising it toward 3600 mints more often, at 3599 once for every command; lowering it hands out a token a long command outlives. Where it loses: one `gh` or `git` command that runs longer than half an hour, started as its token's last half hour began, is refused midway, where a shorter-lived command, or a token minted afresh, would not be. Decided 2026-10-06 (asdlc-openspec-owva.4).
